# Implicit methods (SDF-based)
Also called: Implicit representation, MLP Implicit Surface Representation, Neural Implicit Surface

## Overview
Implicit methods parameterize scene features (density, color, occupancy probability, SDF value) as a continuous function approximated via an MLP network, allowing for high accuracy at arbitrary resolutions [S1]. Unlike explicit methods (voxels, point clouds, meshes) which are discrete and limited in resolution, implicit methods are continuous and accurate at arbitrary resolutions [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves representing the 3D scene using an implicit function (e.g., SDF) approximated by a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) [S1]. The network maps 3D coordinates in object space to a continuous output value. This continuous nature allows the representation to be evaluated at any resolution without the discretization artifacts inherent in voxel grids or the topological constraints of meshes [S1].

## Subtopics

### Implicit Neural Networks (Neural Fields)
Implicit neural networks, also known as neural fields, use implicit neural networks as continuous measurement representations [S2, unofficial]. They are naturally differentiable with respect to input coordinates, allowing gradient-based optimization of measurement coordinates [S2, unofficial]. Compared to splines, implicit neural networks perform as well but require more time to optimize and are less simple to interpret [S2, unofficial].

## Background
Implicit methods emerged as a response to the limitations of conventional reconstruction methods that represented 3D scenes explicitly using grids of voxels, point clouds, or meshes, which resulted in discrete shapes at limited resolution [S1]. Key developments include IM-NET (Chen et al. 2019), which trains the network through deep learning using VAE+GAN, replacing traditional reconstruction with a new implicit surface function decoder during single-view 3D modeling to improve effectiveness and efficiency [S1]. Occupancy Networks (Mescheder et al. 2019) also contributed to this area [S1].
